title: The auction
summary: Your boots from your first goal are in a charity auction online. With ten minutes to go, someone called BOOTS4EVER is bidding against your dad. A season on, you find out who BOOTS4EVER is.

ends.title: Dad's boots
ends.text: Your dad paid far too much for your old boots at a charity auction, bidding against a man with a tiny car. They're on his mantelpiece.

ends.title: The other bidder
ends.text: Your old boots went to a man who bid against your dad at a charity auction. He sends you a photo of them once a year.

beats.title: Ten minutes

event.title: Ten minutes
event.speaker: dad
setup: Your boots from your first goal are in the hospice's online auction. Ten minutes left. {dad.short} rings you in a state. "Someone called BOOTS4EVER keeps outbidding me. Who is BOOTS4EVER?"

say: "It's at four hundred. Your mum says I'm not allowed over five. It's for charity, so it doesn't count, does it?"

replies.label: "Go to six. I'll give you the difference."
"I'll give you a pair I've worn this season."

won.text: He wins at six hundred and forty with one second left, then rings back to tell you about the one second. Twice. The hospice gets a new kettle and a lot more.

lost.text: BOOTS4EVER wins at four hundred and ten. Your dad says he's fine about it in the voice he uses when he isn't.

new.text: "It's not the same," he says, and lets BOOTS4EVER win. The new pair goes on his mantelpiece. He tells people they're the old ones.

beats.hint: Your old boots are for sale

beats.title: BOOTS4EVER

event.title: BOOTS4EVER
event.speaker: dad
setup: A season on. A message from a stranger: a photo of your old boots on a shelf in a tiny flat, next to a photo of a boy in your shirt. "BOOTS4EVER here. My lad's nine. Thought you'd want to know where they ended up."

choices.label: Reply and ask about his lad.

outcomes.text: He was the other bidder. He's not bitter. He's bought the lad a ticket for Saturday with the money he didn't spend. You leave two more at the gate.
His lad plays left wing for the under-tens. You send a signed card. Your dad, when you tell him, goes very quiet and then says, "Good."
Your dad rings him. They talk for an hour about the one second. Now they're mates.
Your dad reads it twice. "Fair enough," he says. "Good home."

beats.hint: A season on, the other bidder
